headline: American Electric Power plans to invest about $4 billion in a fuel cell power plant in Wyoming to supply electricity to Google.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a large utility-built power deal for a data center, though only a plan.
importance_line: Google and AEP investors are most directly affected and communities near Cheyenne will see a large new power plant, but it is a plan with full operation not targeted until the end of 2028.
summary: Tech Insider reports, citing AEP's announcement of 14 Oct 2026, that the utility will own about 92 percent of a 702-megawatt plant near Cheyenne that uses Bloom Energy fuel cells, which make electricity chemically rather than by burning fuel, with Google buying the power under a 20-year contract and full operation targeted for the end of 2028. Tech Insider notes it is unusual for a regulated utility to build and own generation for a single technology customer.
notes: CoStar original blocked; read Tech Insider's report of the AEP announcement. Reuters and Quartz carry the story by headline.
